Keywords: icon button accessibility label accessibilityLabel contentDescription
Description: Icon-only buttons must expose an accessible label
Do: Give icon-only buttons an accessibility label (SwiftUI accessibilityLabel, Compose contentDescription)
Don't: Icon buttons without accessible names
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: Button(action: close) { Image(.closeIcon) }.accessibilityLabel("Close") | Compose: IconButton(onClick = close) { Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = "Close") }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Button(action: close) { Image(.closeIcon) } | Compose: IconButton(onClick = close) { Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = null) }

Description: All inputs must have a visible label and an accessibility label
Do: Pair a visible label with the field; the label is also its accessibility name
Don't: Inputs with placeholder only
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: LabeledContent("Email") { TextField("name@example.com", text: $email) } | Compose: OutlinedTextField(value = email, onValueChange = onEmail, label = { Text("Email") })
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: TextField("Email", text: $email) // placeholder is the only label | Compose: TextField(value = email, onValueChange = onEmail, placeholder = { Text("Email") })

Description: Interactive elements must expose correct roles/traits
Do: Use real controls (Button, Toggle, Link) or set the role explicitly
Don't: Rely on generic views with no roles
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: Button("Submit", action: submit) | Compose: Button(onClick = submit) { Text("Submit") }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Text("Submit").onTapGesture(perform: submit) | Compose: Text("Submit", Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) { detectTapGestures { submit() } })

Keywords: live region announce accessibility announcement status
Description: Async status updates should be announced to screen readers
Do: Announce status changes (SwiftUI AccessibilityNotification.Announcement, Compose liveRegion)
Don't: Update text silently with no announcement
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(status).post() | Compose: Text(status, Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite })
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Text(status) // changes silently | Compose: Text(status) // changes silently

Description: Decorative icons should be hidden from screen readers
Do: Hide decorative icons from the accessibility tree
Don't: Have screen reader read every icon
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: Image(decorative: "sparkle") | Compose: Icon(painter, contentDescription = null)
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Image("sparkle") // reads the asset name | Compose: Icon(painter, contentDescription = "sparkle")

Keywords: touch target size platform iOS 44pt Android 48dp web 24 CSS px minimum frame minimumInteractiveComponentSize
Description: Native targets use 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android; web WCAG 2.2 has a separate 24 by 24 CSS px minimum with exceptions
Do: Select 44pt for iOS and 48dp for Android at runtime; evaluate web targets separately against WCAG 2.5.8 and its exceptions
Don't: Collapse iOS 44pt, Android 48dp, and web 24 CSS px into one cross-platform number
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(.rect) | Compose: Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize() // 48dp; web: evaluate 24 CSS px + WCAG exceptions
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Image(systemName: "xmark").font(.caption2).onTapGesture(perform: close) | Compose: Icon(icon, null, Modifier.size(16.dp).clickable(onClick = close))

Description: Adjacent touch targets need enough spacing
Do: Keep at least 8pt (8dp) spacing between touch targets
Don't: Cluster many buttons with no gap
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: HStack(spacing: 8) { … } | Compose: Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) { … }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: HStack(spacing: 0) { … } | Compose: Row { … } // no gap

Description: Custom gestures must not break system scroll/back
Do: Reserve horizontal swipes for carousels
Don't: Full-screen custom swipe conflicting with back
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: paged TabView inside a vertical ScrollView | Compose: HorizontalPager inside a vertical scroll
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: DragGesture over the whole screen fighting the edge-swipe back | Compose: full-screen pointerInput drag blocking predictive back

Description: Back navigation should be predictable and preserve state
Do: Pop the navigation stack and keep screen state
Don't: Reset stack or exit app unexpectedly
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: dismiss() // @Environment(\.dismiss) | Compose: backStack.removeLastOrNull() // Navigation 3
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: path = NavigationPath() on the first back | Compose: activity.finish() on the first back

Description: Bottom tab bar should have at most 5 primary items
Do: Use 3–5 tabs and move extras to More/Settings
Don't: Overloaded tab bar with many icons
Code Example Good: Home/Explore/Profile/Settings
Code Example Bad: Home/Explore/Shop/Cart/Profile/Settings/More

Description: Modals/sheets must have clear close actions
Do: Provide a close button and the platform dismiss gesture (swipe down, back)
Don't: Trapping users in modal with no obvious exit
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .sheet(isPresented: $shown) { NavigationStack { Content().toolbar { Button("Close") { shown = false } } } } | Compose: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = onClose) { … }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: .fullScreenCover with no close button | Compose: Dialog(onDismissRequest = {}, properties = DialogProperties(dismissOnBackPress = false)) { … }

Description: Returning to a screen should restore its scroll and form state
Do: Keep each tab alive with its own stack, or save its state
Don't: Reset list scroll and form inputs on every visit
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: TabView with a NavigationStack per tab; @SceneStorage for drafts | Compose: per-tab back stacks; rememberSaveable and hoisted LazyListState
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: switch tab { case .home: HomeView() } // rebuilt on every switch | Compose: when (tab) { … } without saved state

Description: Show visible feedback during network operations
Do: Use a progress indicator or skeleton for >300ms operations
Don't: Leave button and screen frozen
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: if loading { ProgressView() } else { Button("Save", action: save) } | Compose: if (loading) CircularProgressIndicator() else Button(onClick = save) { Text("Save") }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Button("Save", action: save) // no loading state | Compose: Button(onClick = save) { Text("Save") } // no loading state

Description: Confirm successful actions with brief feedback
Do: Show a snackbar, checkmark or banner
Don't: Complete actions silently with no confirmation
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: brief "Saved" banner or checkmark overlay | Compose: snackbarHostState.showSnackbar("Saved")
Code Example Bad: // silently update state only

Description: Show clear error messages near the problem
Do: input-level error + summary banner
Don't: Only change border color with no explanation
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: TextField(…) with Text(error) right under it | Compose: OutlinedTextField(value = email, onValueChange = onEmail, isError = true, supportingText = { Text(error) })
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: TextField(…).border(.red) // no message | Compose: OutlinedTextField(value = email, onValueChange = onEmail, isError = true) // no message

Description: Validate inputs on blur or submit with clear messaging
Do: Validate when the field loses focus and on submit
Don't: Validate on every keystroke causing jank
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .onChange(of: focused) { _, isFocused in if !isFocused { validate() } } | Compose: Modifier.onFocusChanged { if (!it.isFocused) validate() }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: .onChange(of: email) { validate() } // every character | Compose: onValueChange = { email = it; validate(it) } // every character

Description: Use appropriate keyboardType and returnKeyType
Do: Match email/tel/number/search keyboards
Don't: Use default keyboard for all inputs
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .keyboardType(.emailAddress).textContentType(.emailAddress) | Compose: keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email)
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: default keyboard for every field | Compose: default KeyboardOptions for every field

Keywords: focus next field submit label ime action
Description: Guide users through form fields with Next/Done flows
Do: Move focus to the next field on Next and submit on Done
Don't: Force users to tap each field manually
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .submitLabel(.next).onSubmit { focus = .password } | Compose: keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Next), keyboardActions = KeyboardActions(onNext = { focusManager.moveFocus(FocusDirection.Down) })
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: // no onSubmit, manual tap only | Compose: // no keyboardActions, manual tap only

Keywords: secure field password show hide toggle
Description: Allow toggling password visibility securely
Do: Provide a Show/Hide toggle next to the password field
Don't: Force users to type blind with no option
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: SecureField or TextField switched by an eye Button | Compose: visualTransformation = if (shown) VisualTransformation.None else PasswordVisualTransformation() + trailingIcon toggle
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: SecureField with no toggle | Compose: PasswordVisualTransformation() with no toggle

Keywords: lazy list virtualization List LazyVStack LazyColumn
Description: Use lazy lists for lists over ~50 items
Do: Use List or LazyVStack and LazyColumn with stable keys
Don't: Render hundreds of items eagerly
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: List(items) { ItemRow(item: $0) } // Identifiable | Compose: LazyColumn { items(items, key = { it.id }) { ItemRow(it) } }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: ScrollView { VStack { ForEach(items) { ItemRow(item: $0) } } } | Compose: Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(state)) { items.forEach { ItemRow(it) } }

Description: Use correctly sized and cached images
Do: Load images at display size and cache them
Don't: Load full-resolution images everywhere
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: AsyncImage(url: thumbnailURL) { $0.resizable().scaledToFill() } placeholder: { ProgressView() }.frame(width: 40, height: 40) | Compose: AsyncImage(model = thumbnailUrl, contentDescription = null, contentScale = ContentScale.Crop, modifier = Modifier.size(40.dp))
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: full-resolution 4K image for a 40pt avatar | Compose: full-resolution 4K image for a 40dp avatar

Description: Debounce scroll/search callbacks to avoid jank
Do: Wrap handlers with debounce/throttle
Don't: Run heavy logic on every event
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .task(id: query) { guard (try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(300))) != nil else { return }; await search(query) } | Compose: snapshotFlow { query }.debounce(300).collectLatest { search(it) }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: search on every keystroke | Compose: search on every keystroke

Description: Micro-interactions should be 150–300ms with native-like easing
Do: Use ease-out for enter/ease-in for exit
Don't: Use long or linear animations for core UI
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2)) { … } | Compose: tween(durationMillis = 200, easing = FastOutSlowInEasing)
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.8)) { … } | Compose: tween(durationMillis = 800, easing = LinearEasing)

Description: Respect OS reduced-motion accessibility setting
Do: Check the system reduce-motion setting and simplify animations
Don't: Ignore user motion preferences
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion); withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring) { … } | Compose: Settings.Global.getFloat(contentResolver, Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE, 1f) == 0f → skip the animation
Code Example Bad: Always run complex parallax animations

Description: Reserve infinite animations for loaders and live data
Do: Use looping only where necessary
Don't: Keep decorative elements looping forever
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: ProgressView() only while loading | Compose: CircularProgressIndicator() only while loading
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: .repeatForever() bounce on background icons | Compose: rememberInfiniteTransition() on decorative icons

Keywords: font size dynamic type body text style
Description: Body text must be readable and support Dynamic Type
Do: Use text styles that scale; body at least 16pt (16sp)
Don't: Render critical text below 12pt
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: Text("Body").font(.body) | Compose: Text("Body", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge) // 16sp
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: Text("Body").font(.system(size: 10)) | Compose: Text("Body", fontSize = 10.sp)

Keywords: dynamic type font scale large text
Description: Support system text scaling without breaking layout
Do: Let text scale with the system setting and test the largest sizes
Don't: Clamp text size or fix the height of text containers
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .font(.body) and @ScaledMetric for spacing next to text | Compose: sizes in sp and Modifier.heightIn(min = …) instead of a fixed height
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: .dynamicTypeSize(.large) on the root view | Compose: Modifier.height(40.dp) around a label

Description: Content must not overlap notches/gesture bars
Do: Keep content inside safe areas and window insets
Don't: Place tappable content under system bars
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: content inside the safe area; only backgrounds use .ignoresSafeArea() | Compose: Scaffold { padding -> Content(Modifier.padding(padding)) } or Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: .ignoresSafeArea() on tappable content | Compose: edge-to-edge without applying insets

Description: Ensure sufficient contrast in both light and dark themes
Do: Use semantic tokens and test both themes
Don't: Reuse light-theme grays directly in dark mode
Code Example Good: colors.textPrimaryDark = '#F9FAFB'
Code Example Bad: colors.textPrimaryDark = '#9CA3AF' on '#111827'

Description: Don't rely solely on hidden gestures for core actions
Do: Provide visible buttons in addition to gestures
Don't: Rely on swipe/shake only with no UI affordance
Code Example Good: Swipe to delete + visible Delete button
Code Example Bad: Only shake device to undo with no UI

Keywords: accessible drag interaction drag single pointer alternative reorder resize move buttons accessibility actions iOS Android
Description: Drag and reorder operations need a non-drag path
Do: Provide named Move up/down buttons or a position menu beside drag handles, and expose them as accessibility actions
Don't: Make drag or swipe the only way to reorder native content
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: .accessibilityAction(named: "Move up") { move(index, index - 1) } | Compose: Modifier.semantics { customActions = listOf(CustomAccessibilityAction("Move up") { move(index, index - 1); true }) }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: drag handle only | Compose: drag handle only

Keywords: password manager passkey paste redundant entry
Description: Authentication and multi-step flows should reuse prior values
Do: Support password managers passkeys paste and prefilled confirmed values
Don't: Force users to retype credentials or the same data in one flow
Code Example Good: SwiftUI: SecureField("Password", text: $password).textContentType(.password) | Compose: Modifier.semantics { contentType = ContentType.Password }
Code Example Bad: SwiftUI: paste blocked, no content type | Compose: paste blocked, no content type
